_comment: Real `yt-dlp -J` output for https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw, captured on 2026-08-16 from the yt-dlp version recorded in `_captured_from_yt_dlp` below, and trimmed to what the app actually reads. This exists because every other gate in this repository checks the app against itself: nothing compares the field names in models/yt_dlp.rs against what yt-dlp really emits, so a renamed or retyped field upstream passes cargo test, clippy, the coverage floor and both release self-checks, and reaches the user as a download that fails with no local explanation. Trimming is deliberate and so is what survived: three formats covering the shapes the code branches on (a muxed one, a video-only one with acodec none, an audio-only one with vcodec none), and a filesize of null next to a populated filesize_approx. Two things were edited rather than captured verbatim: the thumbnail query string (an expiring signature, irrelevant to parsing) is dropped, and comments is absent here because it is absent from real -J output too, which is the point of the assertion about it. Refresh with the ignored live-contract test that re-fetches this; do not hand-edit a field name into agreement. What tells you a refresh is due is the weekly `yt-dlp fixture freshness` job in scheduled-audit.yml, which compares the version below against yt-dlp's latest release and opens an issue when they differ. It cannot check the contract itself: that needs a real YouTube fetch, and YouTube refuses a datacenter IP with a bot check, so the verification stays a local step and only the reminder is automated.
